message.content:
Here’s a quick roundup of some of the most highly regarded crime‑thriller films released in 2020 (in no particular order):

| Film | Director | Notable Cast | Why It Stands Out |
|------|----------|--------------|-------------------|
| **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | A modern twist on the classic horror tale, it blends psychological suspense with social commentary on abuse and gaslighting. |
| **Tenet** | Christopher Nolan | John David Washington, Robert Pattinson | Though more sci‑fi, its intricate time‑travel plot and high‑stakes espionage give it a crime‑thriller edge. |
| **The Trial of the Chicago 7** | Aaron Sorkin | Eddie Redmayne, Sacha Baron Cohen | A courtroom drama that doubles as a political thriller, capturing the tension of the 1969 protest trial. |
| **The Gentlemen** | Guy Ritchie | Matthew McConaughey, Charlie Hunnam | Ritchie's signature fast‑paced storytelling and witty dialogue make this gangster caper a standout. |
| **Uncut Gems** | Josh & Benny Safdie | Adam Sandler, Kevin Garnett | Sandler’s manic performance and the film’s relentless pacing create an adrenaline‑filled heist thriller. |
| **The Irishman** | Martin Scorsese | Robert De Niro, Al Pacino, Joe Pesci | Scorsese’s epic saga of organized crime spans decades, blending historical narrative with deep character study. |
| **The Hunt** | Thomas Vinterberg | Mads Mikkelsen, Nikolaj Coster-Waldau | A tense cat‑and‑mouse chase across rural Denmark, exploring themes of paranoia and betrayal. |
| **The Night House** | David Bruckner | Rebecca Hall, Nathan Lane | A psychological thriller that uses supernatural elements to explore grief and domestic abuse. |
| **The Last Duel** | Ridley Scott | Matt Damon, Adam Driver | While historically based, the film’s duel‑driven plot and moral ambiguity give it a crime‑thriller feel. |
| **The Platform** | Galder Gaztelu-Urrutia | Iván Massagué, Zorion Eguileor | A dystopian allegory that turns into a brutal survival thriller, critiquing class disparity. |

These selections cover a range of sub‑genres—from heists and gangland sagas to courtroom dramas and psychological thrillers—making them great picks for anyone looking to dive into crime‑thrillers from 2020.
